column3: “In the midst of the tent” is rendered “inside the tent,” and “brought near” as “offered.”
“From man and unto woman” is rendered “both man and woman.” The second food item is rendered “a portion of meat”; the meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain (others take it as a date cake).
“Servants” is rendered “ministers,” and “to make remembrance” as “to celebrate.”
“Instruments of lyres and with harps” is rendered “musical instruments, harps, lyres,” with the two stringed instruments reversed; NASB supplies “played.”
“By the hand of Asaph” is rendered as “assigned Asaph … to give thanks”; NASB supplies “assigned.”
“Proclaim in his name” is rendered “call upon His name.”
“Tell in all his wonders” is rendered “Speak of all His wonders.”
“His wonders” (the first) is rendered “His wonderful deeds,” and “the judgments of his mouth” as “the judgments from His mouth.”
The Hebrew has “you” here; NASB reads “they,” as in Psalm 105:12. “Men of number” is rendered “only a few in number,” and “like a few” as “very few.”
“Rebuked” is rendered “reproved,” and “on them” as “for their sakes”; NASB supplies “saying.”
“Recount” is rendered “tell of,” and “wonders” as “wonderful deeds.”
“Worthless idols” is rendered “idols”; the Hebrew word plays on “gods.”
NASB supplies “due”; “lift up an offering” is rendered “bring an offering,” and “adornment of holiness” as “holy array.”
“Also it is established” is rendered “Indeed, the world is firmly established”; “shaken” is rendered “moved.”
